chapter: Streetcar, Cab revival shows and trips abroad
title: Dating Streetcar Named Desire and how the job was first offered
summary: Sorting out dates with the Encyclopedia, he places Endorsed by Dorsey in 1947 and Streetcar in 1947-48. An agent called him to form a group, but his price was undercut and Willie the Lion Smith was lined up.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: There was one more thing I wanted to ask you about and that was, because you'd gotten up to Cy Oliver, what about when you were with Street Car Named Desire?

This is why -- I went from Cy after we went in this thing, I got this thing with Street Car Named Desire and I became the musical director of Streetcar Named Desire. And that's when I left Cy and went into Streetcar Named Desire.
Oh, because you had said Cy was in the -- according to the Encyclopedia it says, Endorsed by Dorsey show, WOR, in '48, '49. Conductor and arranger for the band Streetcar Named Desire.
It says Cy Oliver, Zanzibar, '50. I see, Streetcar was '47, '48? How did that come about?
'47 was when we did the Endorsed by Dorsey Show.
Then you went from there into Streetcar?
Then I went from there into Streetcar Named Desire.

Well, that came about -- I can't think of the man, an agent, that called me for this thing. Can't think of his name. But anyway, I wish I could think of it because I can see his face right now. But he called me and asked me would I like to -- could I get a group together for Streetcar Named Desire. And I went over to his office and we talked about it and he said, how much would it cost? So I told him it would cost him -- it would be four or five pieces and I said it would be $500.00 a week a man, $1,000.00 for me as the leader. Okay.

So this went on until it finally boiled down. I didn't hear from him again and I called him and he told me that John Hammond -- this is what he told me -- told him he didn't have to pay that much money for musicians and that he could get him some people. So Willie the Lion Smith was supposed to take it over. And George Avakian (PHONETIC) became the booker.
We're going to stop now for --
